title: A dual-threshold system relying on multiple c-di-GMP metabolic enzymes controls cell fate of a cyanobacterium
experiments_summary: The study employed systematic genetic, biochemical, and cell biological methods in Anabaena sp. PCC 7120. (1) Mutant construction: All 8 phosphodiesterase (PDE) genes were sequentially deleted using CRISPR-Cpf1 to generate a PDE-null strain (cdGmax) and seven intermediate strains (1ΔPDE–7ΔPDE). Similarly, all 14 GGDEF-domain genes were sequentially deleted to attempt a DGC-null strain; the final gene (all1219) was placed under a Cu2+/theophylline-inducible CT promoter in the 13ΔDGC background to generate a conditional cdG0 strain. Twelve intermediate DGC deletion mutants were also generated. Additional double and triple mutants (e.g., ΔcdgSΔalr2306, ΔcdgSΔalr3599CT-all1219, Δ8DGC-1) were constructed to identify dominant enzymes. (2) c-di-GMP quantification: Intracellular c-di-GMP levels were measured by UPLC-MS/MS (LC-MS) in all mutant and wild-type strains, including time-course measurements after inducer removal in conditional strains. Standard curves with known c-di-GMP concentrations were used for absolute quantification. (3) Cell morphology analysis: Cell length and width were measured by light microscopy (SDPTOP EX30) and ImageJ across all strains and time points. (4) Growth assays: Cell growth was monitored by OD750 measurements under BG11 and BG11 minus nitrogen (BG110) conditions. (5) Complementation and overexpression experiments: Heterologous DGC YdeH or its inactive variant YdeHGGAAF was expressed in the cdG0 background; cdgR was deleted in the cdG0 background to test epistasis; complementation strains (e.g., ΔcdgSΔalr2306::alr2306) were generated to confirm phenotypic specificity. (6) Protein purification and enzymatic assays: Full-length CdgS and Alr3599, and a truncated Alr1219 (Alr1219-ΔCT), were expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3) from pHTwinStrep vectors, purified via Strep-Tactin affinity and size-exclusion chromatography, and assayed for DGC activity by HPLC. Michaelis-Menten kinetics were determined using a GTP concentration series (3.13–200 μM), and c-di-GMP feedback inhibition constants (Ki) were determined by preincubating proteins with varying c-di-GMP concentrations (1–100 μM). (7) Transcriptional analysis: qRT-PCR was performed on RNA extracted from ΔcdgSCT-all1219 cells at multiple time points after inducer removal using gene-specific primers to measure alr3599 transcript levels. (8) Western blot analysis: Alr3599-Flag protein levels were assessed by western blot with anti-Flag antibody in the ΔcdgSCT-alr1219 (alr3599-Flag) strain at multiple time points to determine post-translational regulation. (9) CdgR quantification: Absolute intracellular CdgR protein concentrations were determined by immunoblot using purified CdgR as a standard curve, with cell extracts normalized to OD750. Cell volume was estimated geometrically from microscopy measurements to calculate molar concentrations. CdgR/c-di-GMP ratios were calculated for WT and various mutants. (10) Dose-response analysis: Cell size versus c-di-GMP level data from all mutants were plotted to define morphological and viability thresholds; the conditional cdG0 strain was used to titrate c-di-GMP concentrations by varying inducer levels and correlating them with phenotypic outputs. (11) ppGpp pathway assessment: Strains overexpressing or disrupting the relA/spoT homolog All1549 were analyzed for cell size to compare c-di-GMP and ppGpp contributions to cell size control. Statistical analyses used independent-sample t-tests and one-way ANOVA with Sidak's post-hoc test.
